name: India
notes: Depth: seed. Scope: the Union level in every layer reached by web search (think tank and economists behind the 2024 World Inequality Lab proposal, CPI(M) and CPI manifestos, Oxfam India, the Centre for Financial Accountability and Tax the Top campaign, two economists, one Congress leader, the 2020 revenue officers' paper), the 36 states and union territories and 734 districts as a register. First pass R001 and gap pass R002 (2026-10-20). R002 added the Tax the Top petition names and organisations, the campaign's two websites (taxthetop.org read with the headless browser; the older WordPress site and its 2023 op-ed series), the ten central trade unions' 2024 memorandum, the Left parties' joint statement of Feb 2025, CPI(M) and CPI(ML) Liberation manifestos and Central Committee texts (including one in Bengali), the Rozgar Adhikar Abhiyan (Hindi report) and more economists and opinion writers. Hindi, Bengali, Malayalam and Tamil web searches mostly returned Bangladeshi or explainer pages; the Hindi and Bengali finds came from following leads (Nyay Tak, the CPI(M) West Bengal site). Not done: full-text search of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha debates, state assemblies, the full Tax the Top petition list, most media and economists, municipal bodies. The district map uses Survey of India boundaries (CC0 via DataMeet); districts carry Local Government Directory codes, states ISO 3166-2:IN codes.

polls.question: Wealthy people paying a higher tax on their wealth, as a means of funding major changes to our economy and lifestyles
